questions.text: How dependent is the business on any single customer, channel, supplier, or source of revenue — and what is it doing about that?

A.text: The business depends heavily on a single one of these, and this has not been recognised or addressed

B.text: A heavy dependency exists and is recognised, but nothing is being done about it

C.text: Dependencies are identified and monitored, and the most significant is either being actively reduced or deliberately accepted for a stated reason

D.text: No single dependency would be severe enough to threaten the business — or where one exists, it is secured and mitigated

E.text: As D, and the spread across customers, channels and inputs is deliberately managed rather than an accident of how the business grew

questions.text: When conditions have changed — a market shift, a lost customer, a cost increase, a regulatory change, a competitor move — how has the business responded?

A.text: Conditions have changed and the business has not adjusted

B.text: The business adjusts, but only reactively, once the impact is already being felt

C.text: The business has made deliberate changes in response to changed conditions and can point to specific examples

D.text: As C, and the changes were made early enough to limit the impact, prompted by something the business noticed rather than something it suffered

E.text: As D, and the business watches for the changes that would matter to it, so adjustment is a routine capability rather than an occasional achievement

questions.text: If the business's current path became less viable, does it have other viable routes available?

A.text: The business has one path and no alternative has been considered

B.text: Alternatives are discussed in general terms, with nothing established about whether they would work

C.text: At least one specific alternative route has been identified, with a stated basis for believing it viable

D.text: More than one specific alternative has been identified, and at least one has been tested enough to know it is genuinely available — early conversations, a trial, or an existing capability that transfers

E.text: As D, and the business has actually used an alternative route: served a different customer group, added an offering, or opened a channel — evidencing that shifting path is something it can do rather than something it believes it could

questions.text: Does the business improve or extend what it offers over time?

A.text: The offering has not changed and there is no process for changing it

B.text: Changes happen occasionally, prompted by an individual customer request or a problem

C.text: The business deliberately improves or extends its offering, drawing on what it learns from customers and the market

D.text: As C, and this happens on a recurring basis, with time, people, or budget deliberately allocated to it

E.text: As D, and the business can point to changes that measurably strengthened its position — work won that would not have been won, customers retained that would have been lost, or a new source of revenue opened
